title: Accuracy-vs-labels curve for the best recipe, by strategy, extrapolated to 90/95%
why: Answer 'what does it take to reach 95% accuracy' with an honest label-budget curve and saturating extrapolation.
hypothesis: The label-free adapted score is near the feature ceiling; labels plateau and 0.95 is not within the model family.
data: 160 human OOD labels (138 good/22 bad, 47 factories) + frozen O4 adapted score + 26 per-pixel features; hold-out 108 (92/16, 44 factories) scored once
method: logistic on [adapted,26 feats], StratifiedGroupKFold(5), 4 acquisition strategies x k in {5..160}; error(k)=e_inf+a*exp(-k/tau) fit + 300 fold-bootstrap; hold-out check
summary: Label-free adapted: error 0.267 (BA 0.733, AUROC 0.781) pooled-160 but 0.352 (AUROC 0.676) on the 108 hold-out (does NOT replicate; frozen ensemble 0.690). Label curves plateau ~0.28-0.33; saturating e_inf=0.326 (CI [0,0.384]); k for 0.10 and 0.05 UNREACHABLE. diversity/maximin best at k=80 (0.283); breadth at k=20-60; depth harmful.
decision: Do not promise 0.90/0.95 from labels; report the honest ~0.65 BA hold-out ceiling.

title: Per-factory specialization: per-factory calibration on m labels/factory
why: Test whether a few labels per factory specialize the score enough to move accuracy toward 95%.
hypothesis: Per-factory calibration on 1-4 labels is noise and hurts vs the global model (N1 per-factory normalization failed).
data: 160 OOD labels, 47 factories (~3.4 windows/factory) + adapted score
regime: OOD Egocentric-10K; per-factory, pooled over 40 seeds
method: per-factory Platt / shrunk (partial-pooling) intercept fit on m labels, eval on remaining; m=0..4
summary: Per-factory calibration HURTS: BA drops from 0.733 (global) to 0.52-0.58 at m=1-4; shrunk variant best 0.578 (lam=2), still far below global. Labels/factory to break even is >>4; certifying per-factory 0.05 needs ~1365 labels/factory.
decision: Do not specialize per factory with few labels; keep the global label-free score.

title: Certification budget with the 85-factory corpus at 95% confidence
why: State the exact factory/label count that makes an error bound certifiable with the enlarged corpus.
hypothesis: 85 factories certifies only r~0.20 (grid-union); 0.90 needs ~342 factories, 0.95 needs ~1365.
method: invert UCB = Rhat + sqrt(ln(1/delta')/(2K)) <= r; delta'=delta or delta/46
summary: All 85 factories certifies r=0.200 (grid-union) / 0.133 (single) at 95% confidence; 47 factories only 0.269/0.179. r=0.20 needs 86 factories, r=0.10 needs 342, r=0.05 needs 1365 (grid-union). Corpus is ~16x too small for a 0.05 bound.
decision: Label all 85 factories x 4 windows to certify r=0.20; open a data request for 342/1365 factories for 0.90/0.95.
